---
title: "Methods"
---

The Sacrificial Debt manual pilot uses `codebook/CODEBOOK.md` v0.1.0 as its
controlled coding protocol.

The principal interpretive unit is the proposition. Each proposition must
resolve to stable source coordinates before it can become pilot evidence.
Coordinate records include a `coordinate_scope` field so reviewers can tell
whether `char_start` and `char_end` are relative to the stored segment excerpt,
a full page, a full document, or a complete source capture.
Records may also include `locator_note` for human-readable page, section,
table, item, or folio guidance.

Full page, document, and source coordinate scopes require a matching
`full-text-captures.jsonl` record with captured text, hash, capture method,
capture time, and rights/redistribution status. The current Segall calibration
packet remains `segment_text` scoped because the committed evidence is a
reviewed excerpt, not a rights-reviewed full page OCR capture.

Manual coding proceeds in two layers:

1. Observation records visible textual structure: collective object,
   sacrificers, sacrifice type, alleged survivor or beneficiary, explicit
   comparison, valuation, actor, audience, and date.
2. Interpretation begins only after observation lock and records sacrificial
   asymmetry, creditor/debtor logic, reciprocal obligation, essentialization,
   dischargeability, sanction logic, causal role, rival explanations, and
   evidence strength.

Strong Sacrificial Debt evidence requires all three parts of the A+B+C rule:
identifiable sacrifice, explicit comparison, and a normative implication of
owing, repayment, deserved loss, required contribution, or legitimate sanction.

Rhetoric, reception, and policy remain separate evidence domains. Evidence in
one domain does not automatically establish another.

The first real-source reference packet is treated as pilot calibration until
human review is complete. Project-owner review can establish methodological fit
for this stage, but it is not represented as expert adjudication or final
scholarly authority.
